blocks.text: // SYSTEM ACCESS: LEVEL 100
The complete diagnostic toolkit. Every metric used by institutional investors, decoded.
// Top Line
The raw money a company receives from selling goods. It is the fuel. No revenue = No business.

Desi Logic
The "Galla" (Cashbox). A Kirana shop earning ₹1 Lakh vs ₹5 Lakh. More sales = More activity.
// Core Profit
Earnings Before Interest & Tax. Shows if the actual business model is profitable before paying bankers or government.

Desi Logic
Restaurant earnings minus vegetables & chef salary. If this is zero, shut the shop.
// Bottom Line
The final money left after paying EVERYONE (Staff, Govt, Bank). This is what shareholders own.

Desi Logic
"Haath mein kitna aaya?" Huge sales mean nothing if rent and interest eat everything.
// Your Share
Total Profit divided by total number of shares. It tells you how much profit *your* one share earned.

Desi Logic
If family profit is ₹100 and there are 4 brothers, EPS is ₹25. If EPS grows, you grow.
// The Gold Standard
Measures how efficiently the company uses shareholders' money. >15% is excellent. <10% is poor.

Desi Logic
FD gives 7%. If a business takes your money and generates only 6%, why invest? Look for 15%+.
// Total Efficiency
Return on Capital Employed. It considers both Equity AND Debt. Crucial for heavy industries (Factories, Telecom).

Desi Logic
If you borrow money at 10% interest but your business only earns 8% ROCE, you are destroying wealth.
// Pricing Power
Percentage of revenue left after covering operating costs. High margin = Moat.

Desi Logic
Selling water for ₹20 (cost ₹2) vs selling wheat for ₹20 (cost ₹18). High margin is safer.
// Sales Speed
How many times a company sells its stock in a year. Higher is better.

Desi Logic
Fresh Samosas sold every hour vs Stale bread sitting for a week. Fast movement = Fresh Cash.
// Collection Power
How many days it takes to collect money from customers. Rising days = Bad.

Desi Logic
"Udhaari". If customers pay after 90 days, your cash is stuck. If they pay in 0 days (Cash), you win.
// Leverage
Ratio of total debt to shareholder equity. >2 is dangerous. <0.5 is safe.

Desi Logic
Buying a house with 90% loan vs 10% loan. In a crisis, the guy with 90% loan loses the house.
// Short Term Safety
Current Assets / Current Liabilities. Can the company pay bills due in 12 months?

Desi Logic
Pocket money vs Immediate Bills. You have ₹500, bill is ₹400 (Safe). Bill is ₹600 (Danger).
// EMI Capacity
Operating Profit / Interest Expense. Should be > 3.

Desi Logic
If salary is ₹50k and EMI is ₹45k, you are dead. If EMI is ₹10k, you are alive.
// Real Money
Operating Cash Flow minus Capex (Factory maintenance). The cash actually available to owners.

Desi Logic
Profit on paper is vanity. Cash in bank is sanity.
// Popularity Meter
Price to Earnings. Price you pay for ₹1 of profit. High P/E = High Expectation.

Desi Logic
Buying a shirt at ₹999 vs same shirt at ₹499 during Sale. Low P/E (usually) means Sale.
// Scrap Value
Price to Book Value. Crucial for Banks & Finance companies. <1 means cheaper than assets.

Desi Logic
If you close the shop and sell all furniture, what do you get? That is Book Value.
// Growth Adjusted
P/E divided by Growth Rate. <1 is undervalued. >2 is overvalued.

Desi Logic
Paying ₹1000 for a ticket is fine if it's a Flight (High Speed). Bad if it's a Bullock Cart (Low Speed).
// Rent Income
Dividend per share / Stock Price. The % return you get just by holding.

Desi Logic
Like rent from a house. Even if house price doesn't go up, you get monthly cash.
// Takeover Price
Enterprise Value / Earnings. Better than P/E for debt-heavy companies. It includes Debt in price.

Desi Logic
Buying a house for ₹50L looks cheap, until you realize it comes with a ₹2 Cr unpaid loan.
// Skin in Game
Percentage owned by founders. High is good (>50%). Decreasing is bad.

Desi Logic
Would you eat at a restaurant where the owner refuses to eat? Same logic.
// Danger Signal
% of promoter shares mortgaged to take loans. High pledging is a ticking time bomb.

Desi Logic
The owner has mortgaged his own jewelry (shares) to survive. One crash, and he loses everything.
// Hidden Bombs
Potential debt not on balance sheet (e.g., pending court cases). If they lose, they pay.

Desi Logic
You look rich, but you have a court case worth ₹10 Cr pending. You are risky.
// Fragility
Does 80% revenue come from 1 client? If yes, high risk.

Desi Logic
A tailor who stitches uniforms for only ONE school. If school changes tailor, he is finished.
// Govt Mood
Can one law kill the business? (Alcohol, Mining, Gaming).

Desi Logic
Plastic ban killed plastic bag factories overnight. Don't fight the Government.
// Currency Swing
For export/import companies. If Dollar moves 5%, profit can vanish.

Desi Logic
You earn in Rupees but pay loan in Dollars. If Rupee falls, your loan amount increases automatically.

summary: Metric Armory — the full reference of financial ratios and what each one actually tells you.
